paragraphs.title: The Census in the Plains of Moab

easy.explanation: The passage begins, “And it came to pass after the plague.”
easy.q: When did the LORD speak unto Moses and Eleazar?

easy.explanation: The LORD spoke unto Moses and unto Eleazar the priest.
easy.q: Who was commanded to take the census?

easy.explanation: They were numbered “from twenty years old and upward.”
easy.q: From what age were the men numbered?

answers: To number those able to go to war
medium.explanation: The census included those “able to go to war in Israel.”
medium.q: Why was the census taken?

answers: In the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho
medium.explanation: They spoke with the people in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho.
medium.q: Where did Moses and Eleazar conduct the census?

answers: They were counted by family lines
They were counted by dwelling place
They were counted by the mothers’ ages
medium.explanation: The census was organized according to fathers’ houses and family groups.
medium.q: What does “throughout their fathers’ house” indicate?

answers: It followed the same commanded pattern
It counted the tribe of Levi only
challenge.explanation: The LORD commanded the census as He had commanded Moses and Israel concerning those who came out of Egypt.
challenge.q: How was this census related to the first census?

answers: To identify when it took place
To announce that the plague had begun
challenge.explanation: The opening phrase establishes the timing of the command.
challenge.q: Why does the passage emphasize that the census occurred after the plague?

answers: Both concern men twenty years old and upward
challenge.explanation: The command and its execution both concern men from twenty years old and upward.
challenge.q: What feature is shared by the command and the census itself?

paragraphs.title: Reuben and the Memory of Korah’s Rebellion

easy.explanation: The section begins, “Reuben, the eldest son of Israel.”
easy.q: Which tribe is listed first in this section?

easy.explanation: The families of the Reubenites numbered forty and three thousand and seven hundred and thirty.
easy.q: How many Reubenites were numbered?

easy.explanation: The passage names Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram as the sons of Eliab.
easy.q: Who were the sons of Eliab mentioned here?

medium.explanation: They strove against Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah.
medium.q: In what event are Dathan and Abiram remembered?

medium.explanation: The earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah.
medium.q: What happened to Dathan, Abiram, and Korah?

answers: Their judgment served as a warning and memorial
medium.explanation: The judgment and fire were remembered as a sign to others.
medium.q: What does the phrase “they became a sign” mean in context?

challenge.explanation: The text expressly says, “Notwithstanding the children of Korah died not.”
challenge.q: What surprising fact is stated about Korah’s children?

answers: Dathan and Abiram belonged to Reuben’s families
challenge.explanation: Dathan and Abiram were sons of Eliab, who was listed among Reuben’s descendants.
challenge.q: Why is the account of the rebellion included with Reuben’s family register?

answers: They were swallowed by the earth
challenge.explanation: The fire devoured two hundred and fifty men.
challenge.q: What judgment came upon the two hundred and fifty men?

easy.explanation: The passage begins with the families of Simeon.
easy.q: Which tribe is listed first in this section?

easy.explanation: The families of the Simeonites numbered twenty and two thousand and two hundred.
easy.q: How many Simeonites were numbered?

easy.explanation: Judah numbered threescore and sixteen thousand and five hundred, or 76,500.
easy.q: How many people of Judah were numbered?

medium.explanation: The passage lists the families of Zephon, Haggi, Shuni, Ozni, Eri, Arod, and Areli—seven families.
medium.q: How many families of Gad are listed?

answers: They died in the land of Canaan
medium.explanation: The text says, “Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.”
medium.q: What does the passage say about Er and Onan?

medium.explanation: The phrase introduces the number of people counted in each tribe or family.
medium.q: In these lists, what does “according to those that were numbered” refer to?

challenge.explanation: Judah numbered 76,500, more than Simeon or Gad.
challenge.q: Which of Simeon, Gad, and Judah was the largest?

answers: Families are listed and then a total is given
The division of the land is described
challenge.explanation: Each list names family groups and concludes with the number counted.
challenge.q: What pattern is shared by the lists of Simeon, Gad, and Judah?

answers: The death of Er and Onan
The death of Nadab and Abihu
challenge.explanation: Judah’s list records that Er and Onan died in Canaan.
challenge.q: What genealogical detail is included in Judah’s list?

easy.explanation: The passage lists Issachar and Zebulun before the sons of Joseph.
easy.q: Which two tribes are listed before Joseph’s descendants?

easy.explanation: The text says, “The sons of Joseph ... were Manasseh and Ephraim.”
easy.q: Who were Joseph’s two sons named here?

easy.explanation: Ephraim numbered thirty and two thousand and five hundred.
easy.q: How many Ephraimites were numbered?

medium.explanation: Issachar numbered threescore and four thousand and three hundred, or 64,300.
medium.q: Which tribe numbered 64,300 people?

answers: He had no sons, but daughters
He was a son of Korah
medium.explanation: The passage says Zelophehad “had no sons, but daughters.”
medium.q: What was unusual about Zelophehad’s family?

answers: A family group within a tribe
A place where lots were cast
medium.explanation: Each tribe is organized into named family groups.
medium.q: In these lists, what is a “family”?

challenge.explanation: The text names Manasseh first and Ephraim second.
challenge.q: What order is used for Joseph’s sons in this passage?

answers: Their family identity is carefully recorded
challenge.explanation: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah are named within Manasseh’s register.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by listing Zelophehad’s five daughters by name?

challenge.explanation: Issachar numbered 64,300, more than Zebulun, Manasseh, or Ephraim.
challenge.q: Which was largest among Issachar, Zebulun, Manasseh, and Ephraim?

easy.explanation: These are the four tribes listed in the final part of the census register.
easy.q: Which tribes are listed in this section?

easy.explanation: Dan numbered threescore and four thousand and four hundred, or 64,400.
easy.q: How many people of Dan were numbered?

easy.explanation: The total was six hundred thousand and a thousand seven hundred and thirty, or 601,730.
easy.q: What was the total number of the children of Israel?

medium.explanation: Benjamin numbered forty and five thousand and six hundred.
medium.q: Which tribe numbered 45,600 people?

medium.explanation: The KJV says, “And the name of the daughter of Asher was Sarah.”
medium.q: What was the name of Asher’s daughter?

answers: Organized according to their family groups
medium.explanation: The tribes are counted through their respective families.
medium.q: What does “after their families” mean in these lists?

challenge.explanation: Dan numbered 64,400, more than Asher or Naphtali.
challenge.q: Which of these tribes was the largest?

challenge.explanation: Asher numbered fifty and three thousand and four hundred.
challenge.q: Which tribe numbered 53,400 people?

answers: To give the total census number
To describe the division of the land
challenge.explanation: The verse summarizes the number of all the children of Israel.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the final verse in this section?

easy.explanation: The land was to be divided unto those who were numbered.
easy.q: To whom was the land to be divided for an inheritance?

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “To many thou shalt give the more inheritance.”
easy.q: Who was to receive the greater inheritance?

answers: By drawing lots among families only
easy.explanation: The passage says, “the land shall be divided by lot.”
easy.q: By what means was the land divided?

answers: According to the number of people counted
According to the number of priests
medium.explanation: The many received more and the few received less, according to those numbered.
medium.q: How was the size of each inheritance determined?

answers: The location assigned to each tribe
medium.explanation: The tribal inheritances were assigned by lot.
medium.q: What did the lot determine?

medium.explanation: An inheritance is the portion of land given to a tribe or family.
medium.q: What is an “inheritance” in this passage?

answers: Population determined size, and the lot determined location
challenge.explanation: The size of the inheritance followed the number counted, while the land itself was assigned by lot.
challenge.q: How are population and casting lots combined in the division of the land?

answers: The division was to reflect differences in population
All tribes had the same population
The census had no connection to inheritance
challenge.explanation: The inheritance was adjusted according to whether the group was many or few.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “between many and few” teach?

answers: The first concerns population, and the second determines location
They mean exactly the same thing
The first concerns the Levites only
challenge.explanation: The number of names affected the size of the inheritance, while the lot determined its assignment.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the “number of names” and the “lot”?

paragraphs.title: The Levites, the Priestly Family, and the Census Conclusion

answers: Separately from the families of Israel
easy.explanation: The passage gives a separate register of the families of the Levites.
easy.q: How were the Levites numbered?

easy.explanation: The Levites numbered twenty and three thousand, all males from a month old and upward.
easy.q: How many Levites were numbered?

easy.explanation: The passage names Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun.
easy.q: Who remained from those numbered in the wilderness of Sinai?

medium.explanation: Jochebed bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.
medium.q: Which three children of Amram are mentioned?

answers: They died when they offered strange fire
medium.explanation: Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the LORD.
medium.q: What happened to Nadab and Abihu?

answers: They received no tribal land inheritance among Israel
medium.explanation: The Levites were numbered separately because no inheritance was given them among the children of Israel.
medium.q: What does it mean that the Levites had no inheritance among Israel?

answers: Israel was counted from twenty years, and male Levites from one month
Israel was counted from one month, and Levites from twenty years
challenge.explanation: Israel’s men were counted from twenty years old, while all male Levites were counted from a month old and upward.
challenge.q: What was the difference between the census age for Israel and for the Levites?

answers: They were not part of Israel
They were counted only after the land was divided
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes the Levite census from the census of the children of Israel.
challenge.q: Why are the Levites not included in the total of 601,730?

answers: They died in the wilderness except Caleb and Joshua
challenge.explanation: The LORD had said that generation would die in the wilderness, and only Caleb and Joshua remained.
challenge.q: What does the conclusion say about the generation counted at Sinai?
